cohort: The study included 20 women diagnosed with Morbidly Adherent Placenta (MAP) identified from 42,048 deliveries over a 26-month period, with a mean age of 31.4 years and mean parity of 2.8.
finding: Morbidly Adherent Placenta (MAP) was strongly associated with previous caesarean sections (90%) and placenta praevia (60%), leading to significant maternal complications like massive blood loss, ICU admission (60%), and neonatal complications including prematurity, low birth weight (50%), and a 10% perinatal mortality.
mod_finding: Well-planned caesarean hysterectomy with non-separation of the placenta, adopting a multidisciplinary approach, is recommended as the management option to reduce maternal morbidity and mortality in cases of Morbidly Adherent Placenta.
